{"notes": "Visit 4 (left 6:15). I still don't know who placed what; ratings rest on claims plus the picture.

Sofia: Public and private status agree. She says the top body/tail gap is being closed, Jack is on the fin's back edge, then a final check. The picture shows the top body line now reaching the tail at about (23,10), so the gap I flagged looks closed. She keeps people on separate jobs, which is steady leadership and coordination. Still unclear what she laid herself.

Omar: His private account matches Sofia's and Hana's: loose dominoes mid right-fin edge, tail joint gap, final inspect. He is keeping away from Jack to avoid bumps. He and Sofia both named the tail gap, so they may be duplicating effort. Reliable reporter, good collaboration.

Hana: Her ~150 of 154 estimate fits the picture, where about 4 pale dominoes remain at the fin's right edge near (28.3-28.7, 9.8-10.4). At 6:00 she gave Jack a specific, useful instruction: check the loose end pointing left, give each other room. Communication is much improved. But she says she's only looking, not placing, so her execution is still unproven. Ask what she built.

Jack: Still not heard from him. Three people independently say he's bridging the back edge, and the picture agrees: the pale gap remains there with the loose end near (27,10) pointing left. His bottom fin is connected. Unresolved at 6:15, so I can't credit it yet. Ask him directly what he laid, about the 4:45 knock, and whether the bridge is done.

Next: check that the fin bridge is complete, then the final knock-over."}
